chief_complaint: drinking 1 bottle of wine daily, craving, withdrawal shakes
hpi_details: A 53-year-old male presents to the clinic with drinking 1 bottle of wine daily, craving, withdrawal shakes. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks his morning shakes and tiredness are just from extreme stress and poor sleep, rather than his daily wine habit.
concerns: He is worried that his trembling hands will be noticed by his coworkers and jeopardize his job.
expectations: He hopes to get a prescription nerve tonic or mild sedative to stop the morning hand tremors so he can function at work.
social_hx: Non-smoker; drinks approximately one bottle of wine daily and reports craving and withdrawal tremor.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Alcohol Use Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Alcohol Use Disorder is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes assessment and treatment of alcohol withdrawal before initiating relapse-prevention treatment, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Alcohol Use Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Assess withdrawal severity and history of seizures or delirium; provide medically supervised withdrawal treatment when indicated, then offer counseling and relapse-prevention medication
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: How much alcohol do you drink daily, and has that amount increased over time?
Do you feel a strong urge to drink, or have trouble cutting down?
Do you get shaky, sweaty, or anxious when you go without a drink?
Has drinking affected your work, relationships, or responsibilities?
Have you ever had seizures, hallucinations, or severe confusion when stopping drinking before?

history.answer: I came to the clinic because I can't stop drinking. I finish a whole bottle of wine every single day, and recently my hands have started shaking when I don't drink.
I drink red wine, strictly by mouth. I finish about one full bottle every evening, seven days a week.
I have been drinking socially for years, but over the last few months I started needing an entire bottle just to get the same relaxed feeling.
I had my last glass of wine late last night around eleven o'clock before going to sleep.
I often tell myself I will stop after one glass, but I lose control and drink the whole bottle. During the day, I get strong urges to drink that are hard to ignore.
I tried to stop completely two weeks ago on my own, but the restlessness and craving became so intense that I gave in by evening.
I know I need to cut back, and my wife has been criticizing my drinking. I feel terribly guilty about it, and lately I have felt like having a drink right after waking up.
I've been feeling constantly exhausted and unproductive at my accounting job, and it causes frequent arguments at home. I haven't had legal or financial troubles yet.
No, I make sure never to drive after drinking, and I haven't put myself in dangerous physical situations.
In the mornings I notice my hands trembling, I sweat, feel very anxious, and I've been sleeping poorly. I don't have muscle cramps, runny nose, or diarrhea.
No, I have never had a seizure, hallucinations, or severe confusion when trying to stop drinking.
I have had a couple of patchy memories from heavy evenings, but I have never lost consciousness or overdosed.
No, I have never injected drugs, shared needles, or engaged in high-risk sexual behavior.
No, I haven't noticed yellow skin or eyes, swollen belly, vomiting blood, or dark tarry stools.
No, I don't have abdominal pain, stomach ulcers, or any numbness or burning in my hands and feet.
No, I do not take sleeping pills, tranquilizers, or any prescription pain medications.
No, I don't use marijuana, cocaine, stimulants, or any other recreational drugs.
I have been feeling stressed and low because of my drinking habit, but I don't suffer from severe depression or extreme mood swings.
No, I have never had thoughts of killing myself or harming anyone else.
This is my first time seeking professional medical help, and I have never attended self-help groups like Alcoholics Anonymous.
I am truly determined to quit because I want to protect my health and fix my relationship with my wife, but I realize I need medical guidance.
My wife is supportive of me getting help today, and we live together in a stable home.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like hypertension, diabetes, or liver disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never stayed overnight in a hospital.
I do not take any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or dietary supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I work full-time as an accountant in an office, and I live with my wife.
My father had a drinking problem later in his life, but there is no family history of other major illnesses.

I just assumed the morning jitters and exhaustion were from working long hours and burning out, not the wine I have in the evening. I'm terrified someone at work will see my hands shaking in a meeting and think I can't do my job anymore.
I was hoping you could prescribe a mild pill or nerve medication to stop my hands from shaking during the day.

Fine, bilateral postural tremor visible when hands and fingers are outstretched.
Pupils are symmetric, round, and reactive to light; extraocular eye movements are intact without nystagmus.
